$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the INTERNAL bridge protocol version (MCP server <-> native host <-> extension). This is NOT the MCP JSON-RPC version (that is the date string '2025-06-18', see docs/adr/0007) and NOT the extension release version (the git tag is the release version source, see docs/adr/0026). It is a small monotonically-increasing integer, bumped only when the bridge wire contract (BridgeReq/BridgeResp shape, hello handshake, op/capability semantics) changes incompatibly. Both sides consume this file: src/peer.rs asserts PROTOCOL_VERSION against it in `cargo test`, and scripts/gen-ops.mjs emits it into extension/src/shared/ops.ts.

announce.$comment: LANDED (docs/adr/0027). The extension's self-description, sent unsolicited on connect. Additive and backward compatible, so it did NOT bump protocolVersion: an older server ignores it, and a newer server treats its absence as 'legacy extension, version unknown'.
announce.frame: On connect the extension posts one frame shaped as a BridgeResp on the RESERVED id 0: {id: 0, ok: true, data: {announce: {protocolVersion, version, browser: {name, version}}}}. Server request ids start at 1, so id 0 can never collide with a reply.
announce.whyTheResponseEnvelope: 'Old binary + new extension' is exactly the drift this reports, so the frame must not break a server that predates it. The Rust side deserializes every inbound line into BridgeResp (id/ok required); a bare {type: 'announce'} line would fail to parse, and that error kills the reader loop and drops the connection, leaving the extension to reconnect-loop forever. As a legal BridgeResp it parses everywhere and an older server merely logs an unroutable id.
announce.onDrift: Report, do not enforce. If the extension's release version differs from the host binary's, the server attaches a one-shot advisory to the next tool result telling the agent to ask the user to update. The connection is never refused, and no tool is blocked. Silent when either side reports the 0.0.0 placeholder (a local build; see docs/adr/0026).
announce.protocolVersionUse: Recorded and logged only. See handshake.onMismatch below for the enforcement that is still deferred.

handshake.$comment: STILL INTENDED, NOT WIRED. The announce frame above landed the reporting half; the enforcing half below is deliberately deferred until there is a real protocol v2 to reject — a bug here means no bridge at all. See docs/compatibility.md and docs/architecture.md.
handshake.flow: On connect, the native host -> MCP server exchange carries {hello, protocolVersion, capabilities[]}: after the secret is validated, the extension advertises its available capability ids (from capabilities.json) and its protocolVersion. The server compares protocolVersion and the capability set against what it supports.
handshake.onMismatch: Fail fast: if protocolVersion is incompatible, the server rejects the connection with the PROTOCOL_MISMATCH error (see contracts/errors.json) and a clear message, instead of accepting the connection and only later surfacing a confusing 'unknown op' when a newer/older op is dispatched.
handshake.onMissingCapability: If a tool's required capability (per capabilities.json) is not advertised, the server rejects that tool call up front with a clear message rather than dispatching an op the extension cannot handle.
